liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Don't Ease Me In** (2 reviews): The tape fades in during this opener, so the reported opening guitar noise is missing; Brings this song back for the first time since 1974, in a tight, rocking version with a strong Jerry vocal [4][6]
- **Jack-A-Roe** (1 review): Starts uncertain and nondescript, but Jerry soon makes it his own [5]
- **Looks Like Rain** (1 review): Has some clunky, unlistenable moments but is played with more force than usual [5]
- **I Need A Miracle** (1 other source): Its placement after Drums, leading into Bertha, is uncertain, as is the full setlist [1]
- **Bertha** (1 review): The vocal is forgetful and mumbled on the words [8]

## The recordings

- **gd79-02-07.sbd.cotsman.13879.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 12 songs; 72 min; rated 2.93/5 by 14 [1]. Said about its sound: Recording quality is good but incomplete; The tape is incomplete, with portions of both sets [1][8]
- **gd1979-02-07.set1-sbd.andrewf.86941.flac16**: soundboard; 12 songs; 70 min [2]. Said about its sound: Sound is improved over the earlier copy, though the hiss, tape surface noise and cuts remain [2]

## Around the show

- Steve Parish's book says Jerry took four valiums about thirty minutes before the show [4]
- An attendee says Jerry sat on the drum riser and nodded off while the band played around him [11]
- The next day's papers reportedly blamed a cold and sleepy-making medicine for Jerry's state [11]
- Per Parish, Rock Scully brought four valiums backstage and Garcia swallowed all of them at once [12]
- An attendee says Jerry sat down on stage, then walked off; the crowd yelled and complained [13]
- Parish recalled carrying Jerry up the stage steps after four valiums; Bobby asked what was wrong, and the band left the stage [14]
- The uploader says Jerry's playing and singing worsen as the tape goes on, and links this to Parish's valium account [2]
- The reviewer finds the show better than Parish's account had led them to expect, though still not good [4]
- The reviewer rates it above most of the five-star shows from the 1990s and mid-1980s [6]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd79-02-07.sbd.cotsman.13879.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [1]. Also: The reviewer supplied the roughly 90 minutes that exist; a friend at Carbondale had a deck but no mics; This is all that circulates of the show; no audience recordings had surfaced as of December 2002 [1][7]
- **gd1979-02-07.set1-sbd.andrewf.86941.flac16**: transferred by Andrew F; source: SBD > ? > Cassette provided by Ted Carpenter [2]. Also: This version comes from the same source tape as the earlier 13879 circulating copy [2]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Jerry Garcia: [1979-02-07 Backstage Pass - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/image/1979-02-07-backstage-pass/) [16]
- Poster by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead SIU Arena - February 7, 1979](https://www.dead.net/show/february-7-1979) [17]
